question: True or false: under US law, a trailer showing an actor later cut from the film can be false advertising?
answer: True. In 2022 two viewers sued Universal after renting Yesterday for Ana de Armas, who appears in its trailer but was cut from the film. A federal judge in California ruled that a trailer is commercial speech, an advertisement, so false-advertising law can apply to it. The trailer is a promise.
move: Once something is used to sell, it is judged as a sales pitch.
trap: A trailer looks like part of the creative work, so free speech.
reference: Woulfe v. Universal City Studios LLC, US District Court for the Central District of California, order of December 2022
